title: Large Language Models and Causal Inference in Collaboration: A Survey

bias_targets.methodology: Surveying methods that use causal mediation analysis, counterfactual generation, and the introduction of proxy variables within causal graphs (e.g., structural equation models) to identify and mitigate stereotypical gender associations.

Reviewing techniques that treat bias reduction as a causal inference problem, utilizing methods such as backdoor path adjustment, do-operations on intermediate variables, instrumental variable interventions via reward models, and automated probing benchmarks with specially designed questions and human annotations.

Assessing over-reliance on single modalities in Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) using a curated multi-hop VQA dataset and a causality-enhanced agent framework to mitigate modality-specific biases.
